app.title: Review the risk of your SAE preference list
app.tagline: Add the student's preferences and estimate the risk of remaining without an assignment. This research tool supports decisions; it does not replace or submit the official SAE application.

aboutEstimate.title: About this estimate
aboutEstimate.body: The model uses historical 2024 calibration data and 2025 capacity data. Results are estimates, not official admission guarantees.
aboutEstimate.mtbMode: MTB mode (admission 2026): SHA-256(RUN/IPE+RBD) percentile by school. Results are estimates based on last year's calibration data, not official admission guarantees.

steps.locked: Complete the previous steps to continue.

student.title: 1. Identify the student
student.idHelp: Enter a valid RUN with its modulo-11 check digit, or a nine-digit IPE with its numeric verifier digit. Dots and the hyphen are optional.
student.idHelpLong: Used to compute the SHA-256 percentile specific to each school. Enter a valid RUN with its modulo-11 check digit, or a nine-digit IPE with its numeric verifier digit. Dots and the hyphen are optional.
student.idRequiredHint: Enter the student's RUN/IPE to unlock the analysis.

why.title: Why do we ask for this?
why.body: The identifier is used to reproduce the school-specific MTB tie-break calculation. It does not change or submit the student's official SAE application.
why.privacy: The calculation takes place in this application. A home address is sent to OpenStreetMap only if the family later chooses to geocode it for recommendation distances.

student.situationTitle: Start from the family's current situation

listStatus.label: Is the student's wish list already established?

ties.label: I have not yet decided the exact order between some programs
ties.help: Use this planning option to compare possible orders. The family should still choose the order it genuinely prefers before submitting the official application.
ties.info: Give the same preference-group number to programs the family currently considers tied. The app will compare every compatible order, but this exploratory grouping is not submitted to SAE.

list.title: 2. Build and order the preference list

filters.title: Program search filters
filters.intro: Start with the region and program type. Additional filters are optional.
filters.emptyHint: Leave every filter empty to include all programs.
filters.more: More filters: school day, PIE, PACE, fees and other characteristics
filters.moreHint: Leave a filter empty when that characteristic is not essential for the family.

region.label: Program region
region.help: Choose a region to make the program list shorter. Already selected programs from other regions are kept in the list.

specialty.label: Specialized area
specialty.help: Leave empty to include all specialized areas.

gender.label: Gender composition
gender.help: Leave empty to include mixed, boys-only, and girls-only programs.

schoolDay.label: School day
schoolDay.help: Leave empty to include full-day, morning, and afternoon programs.

rurality.label: Rurality
rurality.help: Leave empty to include both urban and rural schools.

pie.label: PIE integration program
pie.help: Leave empty to include schools with and without PIE.

pace.label: PACE program
pace.help: Leave empty to include schools with and without PACE.

enrollmentFee.label: Enrollment fee
enrollmentFee.help: Leave empty to include every enrollment-fee category.

monthlyFee.label: Monthly fee
monthlyFee.help: Leave empty to include every monthly-fee category.

religious.label: Religious orientation
religious.help: Leave empty to include every orientation.

filters.keptOutside: Existing selected program(s) outside the current filters are also kept available: {n}.

search.title: Search and add programs
search.label: Search for a program
search.placeholder: Start typing the school name, commune, or program details.

current.title: Current preference list
current.empty: No program selected yet. Add the student's first wish above.
current.useBuilder: Use the builder below to enter the existing wish list directly.

order.strictHint: Enter programs in strict order. The first program is the highest-ranked choice, and the final chance of each lower option depends on not getting the options above it.
order.preferenceHint: Add the programs in the order the family genuinely prefers.
order.reorderHint: Use ↑ and ↓ to reorder the student's strict ranking.
order.howBody: Strict ranking means every program has a precise rank. Equivalence classes allow several programs to share the same preference group when the family sees them as tied.

group.label: Preference group
group.hint: Set the same preference-group number for programs considered equivalent. Group 1 is preferred to group 2, etc.
group.longHint: Use the same preference-group number for programs the student considers tied. Lower group numbers are preferred. The app will test every possible order inside each tied group, so families can see whether the exact internal order changes the predicted outcome.

priorities.title: Does the student have priority at this establishment?
priorities.hint: Mark only the situations that apply to this specific establishment. SAE recognizes the four priority criteria below.

descriptions.sibling: Has a sibling enrolled at the establishment
descriptions.student: Has priority-student status for this establishment
descriptions.parentCivilServant: Is the child of an employee of the establishment
descriptions.exStudent: Previously attended the establishment and was not expelled
descriptions.alreadyRegistered: The student is already enrolled in this establishment

priorities.alreadyRegisteredNote: Current enrollment is shown separately because it is not one of the four SAE priority criteria.
priorities.none: No priority declared for this program

notices.imputedTitle: Some selected programs use estimated historical calibration values.
notices.imputedShort: Less reliable estimate: at least one selected program uses mean-imputed 2024 calibration values.
notices.imputedBody: Complete historical observations were unavailable for at least one selected program, so the model uses an imputed 2024 value. Interpret those program-level estimates with additional caution.
notices.removed: Some programs in the current wish list are no longer available in the loaded data and were removed: {programs}
notices.recommendationsAdded: {n} recommended program(s) were added at the end of the list. Check priorities for the new programs, then analyze the list again.
notices.orderCount: The current equivalence classes generate {n} compatible strict order(s). The app will test them to see whether tied programs lead to the same or different predicted outcomes.
notices.addAtLeastOne: Add at least one program to unlock the analysis.
notices.duplicate: That program is already in the list.
notices.maxWishes: The list cannot hold more than {max} programs.

result.title: 3. Review the result
result.heading: Result of the preference list
result.riskLabel: Estimated risk of remaining without an assignment

attention.high: High attention level: consider adding more acceptable programs at the end of the list.
attention.moderate: Moderate attention level: review the list and consider acceptable backup options.
attention.low: Low attention level under the tool's current alert settings.
attention.definitionTitle: How are the attention levels defined?
attention.definitionBody: These are presentation thresholds defined by this research tool, not official SAE thresholds. Low is below {soft}; moderate is from {soft} to below {hard}; high is {hard} or above.
attention.howToRead: How to read this: above {hard}, Unmatched is shown first. Between {soft} and {hard}, it is shown in the podium as a warning. Below {soft}, only schools are shown in the podium.
attention.ordering: Outcomes are always ordered by their estimated probability. The attention alert is displayed separately and never changes this ranking.
attention.hardAlert: Strong unmatched-risk alert: the risk is above the hard threshold. Unmatched is therefore shown as the first outcome. Adding safer options is recommended.
attention.hardNote: The schools listed below Unmatched are still the most likely school assignments, but the unmatched risk is high enough to be treated as the main warning.
attention.softAlert: Moderate unmatched-risk warning: the most likely assignment is {program}, but the unmatched risk is high enough to appear in the podium.
attention.softNote: Unmatched is included here as a warning signal because the risk is above the soft threshold; it is not forced into first place unless the hard threshold is reached.
attention.lowAlert: The student is not flagged as at risk. The most likely assignment is: {program}.
attention.lowNote: The unmatched risk is below the soft threshold, so the podium focuses on school assignments only.
attention.noneAccessible: No listed school appears realistically accessible.

outcomes.title: Most likely estimated outcomes
outcomes.finalChanceFor: Estimated final chance for this outcome: {chance}

detail.trigger: See the detailed calculation for each preference
detail.title: Wish-level details
detail.note: The final chance accounts for every program placed above each preference.
detail.technicalNote: MTB ranks, priority tiers, seats and historical applicant counts are calculation details. They should not be interpreted as official SAE results.

explain.chanceTitle: Chance if considered vs. final chance
explain.chanceBody: Chance if considered is the chance of getting that program if the student reaches that wish. Final chance of assignment also accounts for all higher-ranked wishes. For example, a school can be accessible if considered, but have a lower final chance if the student is likely to get a higher-ranked option first.
explain.chanceShort: Chance if considered estimates access to a program if the student reaches that preference. Final chance also accounts for the possibility of receiving a higher-ranked program first.
explain.percentagesTitle: How should I interpret these percentages?
explain.percentagesBody: This percentage is an estimate based on historical data and model assumptions; it is not an official SAE result or guarantee.
explain.finalChanceNote: A program's final chance accounts for every program placed above it. The unmatched risk is the estimated chance that none of the listed programs is available.

result.strategicNote: Strategic note: adding additional acceptable programs at the end of the wish list does not reduce the student's chance of getting higher-ranked choices. The assignment process considers the list in order and keeps the best available option. Families should therefore add every acceptable backup program, then mark any applicable priority for those added schools and rerun the simulation.

equivalence.title: Equivalence-class sensitivity
equivalence.question: Does the undecided internal order matter?

verdict.stable: The strict ordering inside the equivalence classes does not change the predicted final outcome. All {n} compatible strict order(s) lead to: {outcome}.
verdict.stableProbabilityShift: The strict ordering inside the equivalence classes does not change the most likely school: {outcome}. However, it changes the final assignment probability for that school, from {minChance} to {maxChance} across compatible strict order(s).
verdict.outcomeChanges: The strict ordering inside at least one equivalence class can change the predicted final outcome. The user should choose a strict order carefully for the tied programs.

advice.stable: Changing the internal order does not change the predicted school. The overall unmatched risk also remains unchanged across compatible orders.
advice.stableProbabilityShift: Changing the internal order does not change the main predicted school, but it can still affect the chances of receiving other options. The overall unmatched risk remains unchanged, so the family should still choose the internal order carefully.
advice.outcomeChanges: Changing the internal order can lead to different predicted schools. The overall unmatched risk remains unchanged; only the distribution of assignment probabilities across schools changes.

equivalence.chooseFirst: Inside each tied group, place first the program the family genuinely prefers. The overall unmatched risk does not change, but the most likely school can change.
equivalence.ordersTitle: What each order inside the tied programs leads to
equivalence.placeInOrder: Place the tied programs in this order:
equivalence.onlyTiedShown: Only programs tied within the same preference group are shown below. Programs whose position never changes are omitted.
equivalence.noTiedOrder: No tied-program order was recorded for this option.
equivalence.groupedNotice: Because there are {n} compatible orders, they are grouped below by their most likely outcome.
equivalence.referenceTitle: Detailed calculation for the reference order
equivalence.referenceNote: This reference uses the current row order inside each preference group.
equivalence.referenceIntro: This table shows one reference order: the current row order inside each preference group. The sensitivity test below then checks every strict order that is compatible with the groups. This matters because tied programs can still lead to different predicted schools.
equivalence.technicalTitle: Technical details of all tested orders
equivalence.technicalNote: This technical table contains the complete strict ranking for every tested permutation. It is not needed to choose the order inside tied groups.

improve.title: 4. Improve the preference list
improve.heading: 4. Recommended similar programs
improve.subtitle: Suggested programs
improve.findSimilar: Find additional programs similar to the current wish list
improve.methodBody: Suggestions combine similarity to the current list, approximate proximity, historical demand, estimated admission access and diversity between recommendations.
improve.methodBodyAlt: Recommendations combine revealed preferences, proximity, portfolio-risk improvement, and a diversity step to avoid near-duplicates.
improve.methodNote: Each suggestion is evaluated as if it were added at the end of the list and without any special priority. Adding it higher or declaring a real priority can change the result.
improve.marginalNote: Each recommended program is evaluated as if it were appended after the current wish list. "Chance if considered" is conditional on the student reaching that wish. The marginal unmatched-risk reduction is the current unmatched risk multiplied by that conditional chance; it is also the estimated final assignment chance for a program appended at the end. Projected unmatched risk is the current risk minus that reduction.
improve.portfolioNote: Portfolio-risk estimates are marginal: they assume the program is appended after the current list. Reordering it higher would change final probabilities and should be tested by adding it to the wish list and rerunning the simulation.
improve.priorityNote: Recommended programs assume no special priority flags for the newly added school. If the student has a sibling, priority-student quota, civil-servant, former-student, or already-enrolled priority for that school, add the program to the list and mark the priority before rerunning the simulation.
improve.strategicNote: Adding an acceptable program at the end does not reduce the chance of receiving a higher-ranked preference. After adding programs, verify priorities and analyze the list again.
improve.selectHint: Select only programs the family would genuinely accept. Recommendations are options to investigate, not automatic choices.

address.heading: Home address for distance calculation
address.label: Student home address
address.help: Optional. Used only to compute distance/proximity to recommended programs. If left empty, proximity is estimated from the current wish list. The address is geocoded with OpenStreetMap/Nominatim when you click the button.
address.hint: Enter an address, then click the button to compute recommendation distances from home instead of the current wish-list centroid.
address.intro: Enter a home address to measure distance from home. Otherwise, distance is estimated from the current preference list.
address.changed: Address changed. Click the button to update the coordinates.
address.confirmed: Distances will be computed from the confirmed address: {address}
address.privacyBody: The address is sent to OpenStreetMap/Nominatim only after the family clicks the geocoding button. Distances remain approximate and do not represent travel time.

precision.approximate: The geocoded location is approximate. Distances should be interpreted carefully.
precision.city: The geocoder could only identify the city or municipality. Distances are approximate.
precision.streetNumberUnconfirmed: The geocoder found the street, but could not confirm the exact street number. Distances are computed from an approximate street-level location.
precision.street: The geocoder found the street, but not an exact address point. Distances are computed from an approximate street-level location.
precision.generic: The geocoder returned only an approximate location. Distances should be interpreted carefully.

distance.note: Distances are straight-line estimates. They do not represent road distance, travel time, or actual accessibility.
distance.coordsNote: Distances are straight-line estimates. School coordinates are preferred; commune and regional locations are approximate fallbacks.
distance.proximityNote: Proximity uses school-level coordinates when available. Commune and regional coordinates are only soft fallbacks and are never used for hard distance exclusion. To improve precision, add data/commune_coordinates.csv with commune, region, latitude, longitude.
distance.noHardFilter: Because the home location is only city-level or approximate, no hard distance cutoff is applied. Straight-line distance only affects the recommendation score.
distance.hardLimit: The {maxDistance} km straight-line limit is applied only when the program has reliable school-level coordinates. Commune and regional approximations are never used for hard exclusion.

card.chanceIfReached: Estimated chance if the student reaches this preference: {chance}
card.appendPreview: If appended at the end: estimated unmatched risk {current} → {projected}
card.why: Why it appears: it balances similarity to the current list, proximity and estimated admission safety.
card.add: Add this program to the end of my list
card.assumption: This estimate assumes the program is appended at the end and no special priority is declared.
card.riskLegend: Row colors reflect the projected unmatched risk after appending the program: green below the soft threshold ({soft}), orange between the soft and hard thresholds, and red at or above the hard threshold ({hard}).
